paragraphs: Engineering of structures and machines starts with one habit. Take something that has to stay up or has to move, work out the forces on it, and check that it can take them. People study it because every bridge, crane, shelf and gearbox has to pass that check before anyone builds it, and most of the check is arithmetic you can learn.

The course has twelve lessons in four parts. Loads and equilibrium covers splitting forces, turning effects and the forces at the supports of a beam. Structures finds the force in each bar of a truss, then the stress a bar can carry. Beams and stiffness looks inside a loaded beam, at the shear and bending in it and how far it sags. Machines finishes with levers, pulleys, gears, efficiency and power.
Each lesson follows one object, such as a post with ropes tied to it or a steel rod under load, and explains an idea before it asks about it.
outcomes: You'll be able to split a slanted force into parts and find the force that balances a set of forces.
You'll be able to find the reactions at the supports of a loaded beam.
You'll be able to work out the force in each member of a simple truss and say whether it is pulled or pushed.
You'll be able to turn a load into a stress, and a stress into a stretch.
You'll be able to find the speed, force and power at the output of a lever, pulley or gear train.
prerequisites: You should be comfortable with algebra and basic trigonometry, and know forces, Newton's laws, work and energy.
